column1: # Game profile of Mario Kart World (Switch 2, base game v0). In bring-up
# Nintendo EPD's engine (sead / agl / gsys, Phive), SDK 19.3.3 built for the Switch 2 (sdk spec Ounce), NVN2; modules main + subsdk0 (the C library) + sdk.
# Packed from a dump folder (base/ only). Shaders: Shader/*.Nin_Ounce_NVN2.bfsha.zs (BNSH with Ampere code), as Donkey Kong Bananza's.
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = the C library)
# The NPDM declares 64 MB of system resource: virtual address memory, the game takes its memory as address regions of the alias region. The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB
# (Donkey Kong Bananza's pool, not measured here). The game also sets a heap: nninitStartup asks SetHeapSize for 0x1dbc00000 (7.4 GB, the pool less its used memory).
# 256 MB in front + 4 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 7.5 GB heap region
# Maps past the application pool fail and the used memory counts the alias region's pages, as on Horizon: MKW's NinVirtualAddressHeap (main+0x681134) sizes itself by what the
# system reports free, so without this it never let its blocks go (2.4 GB mapped by the fourth race in kartnative's measurements; their profile has the same key)
# agl's render buffer binding wraps its clears in render conditions, as in Donkey Kong Bananza (same agl); without the key a clear-only rebinding can wipe a target before it is read
